blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Warehouse Build Cost in Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed breakdown of warehouse construction costs in Melbourne, including factors like size, location, and fit-out for Southbank businesses planning a new build.
body: Planning a warehouse build in Melbourne for 2026? Costs vary significantly based on size, site conditions, and the level of fit-out you need. For a standard warehouse in the Southbank or outer-industrial areas, expect to pay between $800 and $1,500 per square metre for the shell alone. Fit-out costs add another $200 to $600 per square metre depending on whether you need office space, high-bay racking, or specialised climate control.

Location is a major cost driver. Sites in Southbank or inner-city Melbourne command higher land prices, but offer proximity to transport links and customers. If you're looking at Tullamarine or Footscray, you might save on land but factor in logistics access. Cota Group advises clients to budget for geotechnical surveys, council permits, and environmental assessments — these can add $50,000 to $150,000 to a medium-sized project.

Material costs have stabilised after the post-COVID spikes, but steel and concrete remain volatile. We recommend locking in prices early with your builder. A fixed-price contract from a reputable commercial builder like Cota Group protects you from market fluctuations. Labour costs in Melbourne are competitive, but specialist trades for industrial fit-outs command a premium, especially for electrical and plumbing works.

Don't forget sustainability requirements. The Victorian Building Authority now mandates higher energy efficiency standards for commercial buildings. Solar panels, LED lighting, and efficient HVAC systems can add 10-15% to upfront costs but reduce ongoing power bills significantly. Many Southbank businesses are opting for these upgrades to future-proof their assets and attract tenants.

Timelines also affect cost. A typical warehouse build in Melbourne takes 12 to 18 months from concept to handover. Fast-tracking a project can increase costs by 10-20% due to overtime and expedited permits. Cota Group recommends a realistic schedule to avoid budget blowouts. We've delivered projects on time and on budget for over 20 years by planning meticulously.

Financing your warehouse build? Many commercial lenders in Melbourne offer construction loans with progressive drawdowns. You'll need a fixed-price contract and a detailed timeline to secure funding. Cota Group works closely with your financiers to provide the documentation they need. Get in touch for a free consultation and a tailored cost estimate for your Southbank or Melbourne warehouse project.

blogPosts.title: Design and Construct vs Traditional Contracting: What's Best for Your Commercial Build?
blogPosts.excerpt: Comparing design and construct with traditional contracting for Melbourne commercial projects, with real insights from Cota Group's Southbank experience.
body: Choosing the right delivery method for your commercial build in Melbourne can save time, money, and headaches. Design and construct (D&C) puts one team in charge of both design and construction, while traditional contracting separates the architect from the builder. For Southbank businesses, D&C often wins because it reduces the risk of miscommunication and delays between design and site work.

With D&C, Cota Group manages everything from initial concept to final handover. You deal with one point of contact, one contract, and one set of responsibilities. This means faster decision-making and fewer change orders. Traditional contracting requires you to manage separate contracts with an architect, engineers, and a builder, which can lead to disputes over scope and cost overruns.

Cost certainty is a major advantage of D&C. Because the builder is involved from the start, we can provide a fixed price earlier in the process. Traditional contracts often start with only a concept estimate, and the builder's price doesn't come until design is complete. For a warehouse development in Melbourne, D&C can shave months off the timeline by overlapping design and construction phases.

But D&C isn't for everyone. If you already have detailed architectural plans and want to tender them to multiple builders, the traditional route may suit you. However, for complex industrial projects where constructability is key, D&C ensures the design is buildable from day one. Cota Group has delivered over 100 projects using D&C, from small extensions to large warehouse complexes.

Quality control under D&C is robust. We employ detailed quality planning and improvement practices across all projects, regardless of delivery method. The key is transparency — we share our programme, budget, and quality metrics with you weekly. Traditional contracting can sometimes create an adversarial dynamic where the builder blames the architect for design issues. D&C eliminates that by keeping everything under one roof.

For most Southbank commercial clients, D&C is the smarter choice. It simplifies the process, reduces risk, and delivers cost certainty. Talk to Cota Group about your next project — we'll walk you through both options and recommend the best path for your business. Call 03 8691 5544 to start the conversation.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 Environmental Initiatives for Melbourne Industrial Projects in 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the most effective environmental initiatives for industrial construction in Melbourne, from solar integration to waste reduction, with advice from Cota Group.
body: Environmental sustainability is no longer optional for commercial and industrial projects in Melbourne. With stricter regulations and growing tenant demand for green buildings, Cota Group integrates targeted environmental initiatives into every Southbank project. Here are the top five initiatives that deliver real results for industrial builds in 2026.

First, solar panel integration on warehouse roofs. Large roof areas on industrial buildings are perfect for photovoltaic arrays. A typical 5,000-square-metre warehouse roof can generate over 500 kW of power, cutting energy costs by 30-50%. Cota Group works with accredited solar installers to design systems that maximise yield and comply with Victorian Feed-In Tariff requirements.

Second, LED lighting with smart controls. Industrial lighting accounts for a significant portion of energy use. Switching to LED luminaires with motion sensors and daylight harvesting can reduce lighting energy by 60-80%. For new builds, we install these from day one; for extensions, we retrofit seamlessly. The payback period is typically under two years for Melbourne warehouses.

Third, rainwater harvesting and water-efficient fixtures. Industrial sites use large volumes of water for cleaning, landscaping, and amenities. Installing rainwater tanks for toilet flushing and irrigation reduces mains water consumption by up to 40%. Cota Group also specifies water-efficient taps and fixtures to minimise waste across the facility.

Fourth, sustainable material sourcing. We prioritise suppliers with certified environmental management systems and use recycled materials where possible. For concrete, we specify blends with recycled aggregate; for steel, we use suppliers with high recycled content. This reduces the carbon footprint of your Southbank build without compromising structural integrity.

Fifth, waste management plans during construction and operation. Cota Group implements strict waste segregation on site, aiming for 90% diversion from landfill. We also design waste management areas within the building for ongoing recycling. These initiatives help clients achieve Green Star ratings and attract environmentally-conscious tenants. Call us to discuss your project's green goals.

blogPosts.title: Planning a Commercial Extension in Southbank? Here's What You Need to Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Essential tips for planning a commercial extension in Southbank, including council permits, structural considerations, and how Cota Group delivers on time.
body: Expanding your existing commercial space in Southbank can be a smart way to grow without relocating. But commercial extensions come with unique challenges, from heritage overlays to neighbouring property constraints. Cota Group has delivered numerous extensions in Southbank and the surrounding suburbs, and we know exactly what it takes to get the job done smoothly.

First, check your zoning and heritage status. Southbank has areas with heritage overlays that restrict facade changes and building height. You'll need a planning permit from the City of Melbourne, and possibly a heritage impact report. Cota Group's design team handles all council liaison, ensuring your extension complies with local planning schemes without unnecessary delays.

Structural engineering is critical for extensions. Adding floors or expanding sideways requires careful load analysis, especially on existing foundations. We engage structural engineers early to assess the current building and design a solution that's safe and cost-effective. For Southbank projects, we often work with steel frames for their strength and speed of installation.

Minimising disruption to your business is a top priority. Cota Group sequences construction to keep your operations running. We erect temporary walls, manage noise and dust, and schedule noisy works outside business hours. Our project managers coordinate with your team weekly to ensure nobody is surprised by site activity.

Budgeting for a commercial extension in Melbourne requires realism. Typical costs range from $3,000 to $6,000 per square metre for retail or office extensions, depending on finishes and complexity. Industrial extensions are generally cheaper at $1,500 to $3,000 per square metre. Cota Group provides detailed fixed-price quotes so you know exactly what you're paying before work starts.

Finally, expect the process to take 6 to 12 months from design approval to handover. Fast-track options exist but add a premium. The key to a successful extension is partnering with a builder who understands Southbank's regulatory environment and has a track record of delivering on time. Contact Cota Group to discuss your extension — we'll give you honest advice and a clear timeline.
